title: Terminal velocity
examples: What makes the falling object stop speeding up?
How does the shape of the object affect its terminal velocity?
Can you show me a graph of speed versus time for this?

explain.say: Today we are learning about terminal velocity. Say what terminal velocity means to you.
When an object falls through the air, it does not fall forever faster. Say the air pushes back against it.
This pushing back force is called air resistance or drag. Say as speed increases, this resistance force grows larger.
Eventually, the downward force equals the upward air resistance force. Say this balance point is the terminal velocity. Say the net force becomes zero.
On a velocity versus time graph, this steady speed looks like a flat line. Say this means the acceleration is zero at that point.

faq.q: Why does the object speed up first if air resistance is always there?
faq.a: Initially, the object's weight is greater than the air resistance. The net force is downwards, causing it to accelerate. You might ask what happens when it first starts falling. Another way to ask is why it speeds up at first.
asks: Why does it accelerate at first?
What happens when it first starts falling?

faq.q: Does the object's shape matter for terminal velocity?
faq.a: Yes, the shape greatly affects the air resistance. A streamlined shape, like a bullet, has less drag than a flat sheet. You could also ask how shape affects falling speed. Another way is what makes it fall slower.
asks: How does shape affect falling speed?

faq.q: Is terminal velocity the same for all objects?
faq.a: No, terminal velocity depends on the object's weight and its shape. A heavy, dense object will have a different terminal velocity than a light, fluffy object. You could ask if mass matters for this. Another way is what determines the final speed.
asks: Does mass affect the final speed?

faq.q: What does a flat line on a v-t graph mean?
faq.a: A flat line means the velocity is not changing over time. This indicates that the acceleration is zero at that specific point. You could also ask what zero acceleration looks like on a graph. Another way is why the graph becomes flat.
asks: What does zero acceleration look like?
Why does the graph become flat?

faq.q: Is the air resistance force always proportional to the speed squared?
faq.a: For many objects falling through air, yes, the drag force is proportional to the square of the speed. This is a standard model used in physics. You might ask what the relationship is between drag and speed. Another way is how drag changes with speed.
asks: What is the drag force relationship?
How does drag change with speed?

facts: Terminal velocity is reached when the net force acting on the object is zero.
The force of air resistance increases as the square of the object's speed.
On a velocity versus time graph, constant velocity is represented by a horizontal line.
Objects falling at terminal velocity are not accelerating.

quiz.say: If an object reaches terminal velocity, what is its acceleration?
quiz.why: When the object reaches terminal velocity, the downward force balances the upward air resistance, meaning the net force is zero, and zero net force means zero acceleration.

wrong.0: This is wrong because air resistance is the force that balances the weight, making the net force zero.
wrong.2: This is wrong because weight is a constant force, but the net force is zero, not just the weight.
wrong.3: This is wrong because speed is a measure of how fast it is moving, not the rate of change of motion.

quiz.say: A v-t graph showing a constant speed would look like:
quiz.why: A constant speed means the velocity is not changing over time, which is represented by a horizontal line on a velocity versus time graph.

wrong.0: This suggests the acceleration is increasing over time, which is not the case at terminal velocity.
wrong.2: This shows increasing speed, meaning the object is still accelerating downwards.
wrong.3: This would indicate that the object is slowing down over time.

quiz.say: If the air resistance force increases with the square of the speed, how does this affect the graph?

options.show: It will be a straight line
options.say: It will be a straight line

options.show: It will be a straight line sloping down
options.say: It will be a straight line sloping down

options.show: It will be a flat line
options.say: It will be a flat line

quiz.why: Since the force is proportional to speed squared, the graph of force versus speed will curve upwards, getting steeper as speed increases.

wrong.0: A straight line suggests the force is only proportional to speed, not speed squared.
wrong.1: This would imply the drag force decreases as speed increases, which is incorrect.
wrong.2: A flat line would mean the drag force does not change regardless of the speed.
